items.title: Don Ewell Interview, 1960-12-01
items.q: i was sort of sorry i didn't bring a saee up

ctx.x: Orleans it was real cold up in Baltimore and it was really fantastic to step off the train and see it's beautiful weather and flowers and the architecture and uh yes well yeah and well then I got a job at Marty Burks on Bourbon Street playing solo piano there in the front that's across from the old absence house I played there several weeks did fairly well and I uh from there I went on to uh the Trade Winds was it yeah I worked several other places in New Orleans just as a single not with any of the bands uh no I…

with a constant appreciation of the sound and the phrasing and tone and the drive and the rhythm and at the same time trying to concentrate on my own my own work yeah but did the bunk ever give any little last minute directions before a piece about how many courses or did he always tell you what key it was going to be in or something we always had this set routine if we didn't hear that loud stamp of his foot right before the last chorus we know there's going to be another one or the last i don't mean the last…

I think that was only for a couple of months. Remember once Dr. Bichet, his brother, Sidney's brother, the trombonist, came up. Were you there when he sat in one night? No, I wasn't. Might have been a different engagement or something. I think I even have a photograph. I don't remember if you were in that photo. I don't believe you were. I don't think. Did you ever play with Natty Dominic? Well, he sat in the Beehive. It's a club on the south side of Chicago. I was playing there with Miff Mole and Darnell Howard…
